contexts.text: They induce a torpor on the nerves and fibres, from which break forth very grievous and fatal diseases.
I perceived in myself a sluggishness of speaking with them... SE 3162.
I was aware of their presence by a torpor and dullness.
Such induce a torpor (on the brain), whence come obstructions, from which are the beginnings of many diseases, and also dulnesses.
They induce such a torpor on the members and joints that the man cannot raise himself up from his bed.
The sphere of such with the sick induces a torpor on the members and joints.
In such a life the faculties would become torpid.
All things, being bound up with frost, become torpid.
In proportion as love recedes from man he becomes torpid. DLove 20:2.
They induce on them a torpor in doing good...
a. Their presence induces a torpor even to the extinction of the affection of truth.
